messages:
tanya_sales: Quick heads-up 1: WidgetLabs POC is blocked. Their Console shows traces for some requests but not others; Splunk export rows missing trace_id. During a bulk demo they hit a bunch of 429s. Can we swarm? :ambulance:

harry_se: on it. Can you paste one example request/headers + the forwarder log line? That'll tell if header is sent to us but dropped before HEC.

tanya_sales: pasted from their support ticket (redacted):
```
POST /v1/chat 200
Headers: { Authorization: Bearer REDACTED, X-Trace-Id: d4e5f6, traceparent: 00-d4e5f600000000000000000000000001-01 }
Client log:
[2026-03-21T11:05:10Z] WARN status=429 reason=rate_limit id=req_123 trace=d4e5f6
[2026-03-21T11:05:11Z] INFO forwarder: sent-to-hec status=ok trace=
```

harry_se: that pattern matches headers arriving at our gateway but HEC events missing trace. Two likely causes: (A) exporter didn't attach metadata.trace_id, or (B) their forwarder samples/strips headers for big payloads.

sam_sre: I can run quick checks: (1) verify our export pipeline sets `metadata.trace_id` for org=widgetlabs, (2) inspect the Splunk connector sampling rules, (3) temporarily bump the POC token qps to prevent 429s during demo. Need approval for short-lived bump.

tanya_sales: I can approve a 10-minute increase for the demo.

sam_sre: done 1 1 raised token qps to 6rps for org=widgetlabs for 10m and enabled debug export logging.

deploy-bot: runtime change scheduled: poc-qps-bump -> org-widgetlabs (owner: sam_sre). Canary: 5% traffic.

deploy-bot: canary OK. change rolled to 100% for org-widgetlabs.

harry_se: quick mitigation I can deploy: small export-adapter change to prefer and copy trace header into `metadata.trace_id` (order: metadata.trace_id || X-Trace-Id || traceparent). Deploying to p-prod-canary now (safe, tiny change).

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: export-copy-trace v0.2.0 -> p-prod-canary (owner: harry_se)

deploy-bot: canary health: 9/9 checks passed, 2% traffic routed.

harry_se: canary verified: exported event includes metadata.trace_id=d4e5f6; Splunk HEC rows now show matching id.

tanya_sales: great 1 please send a short runbook I can give the customer.

harry_se: runbook snippet to share:
1) Ensure client preserves either `X-Trace-Id` or `traceparent`. If using an intermediate forwarder that rewrites headers, make it include the trace id in event metadata as `metadata.trace_id`.
2) Create Splunk HEC drain with `map_trace_id=metadata.trace_id`. Example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/drains \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <org-token>" \ 
  -d '{"type":"splunk_hec","url":"https://splunk.widgetlabs:8088/services/collector","token":"HEC_TOKEN","map_trace_id":"metadata.trace_id"}'
```
3) If they need no sampling for the demo, request `trace_sampling: full` (warning: increases export volume).

nina_security: security checklist: confirm HEC endpoint uses TLS and HEC token is scoped to ingest-only. Also record that customer approved the 10m qps bump; we'll log this in the security approvals doc.

tanya_sales: WidgetLabs confirmed TLS + ingest-only token and approved the 10m bump. I'll run a 10-minute call with their ops to walk through header passthrough and the HEC config. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
